_directive: R1 QUESTIONER output, ROUND 2, sweater-vertical self-improvement loop segment T12, target specialist SLUG=yarn (yarn_sourcing_strategist). Adversarial questions that attack the load-bearing joints this specialist CLAIMS (via competency_questions_covered, owns[], decision_procedure, conflicts_and_dominance) but is most likely to answer weakly, staleley, inconsistently, or by over-claiming. This round reads round1_judgment.json and aims at the SURVIVING weak spots it flagged (the two HIGH findings Q3 pilling-FLOOR/WON overclaim and Q9 named-firm-lab over-attribution, plus the med gaps) AND fresh angles not yet probed. Each question names the specific failure mode it probes. Questions are NOT answered here. Honesty binding observed: no fabrication, honesty tags preserved, the three governing blockers (Ludhiana knit+LINK per-piece rate, live blended CAC, forward India duty) stay [UNKNOWN], off-paper economy stays mechanism, cotton duty ~16.5% never ~7%.

questions.q: Round 1 (Q3) softened owns[] so the pilling FLOOR is 'SET at the yarn PO' with the achieved ICI >=3-4 post-wash PASS held [UNKNOWN]-UNTESTED until a PPS swatch. But your OWN quality-spec KB (kb3 node 1256) states the ICI gate is run on 'a PPS swatch in the exact construction (fibre x twist x gauge)' and that 'only the finished construction reveals the real grade' -- i.e. the achievable grade depends on the KNIT gauge/density owned by machines/construction (T3/T8), not the yarn PO alone. So on what basis does the yarn line CLAIM to 'set the FLOOR' at the yarn PO, when your own KB says the yarn PO can only DEMAND a clause whose realised value is co-determined by construction levers you explicitly exclude (kb3 line 20)? Distinguish precisely what the yarn PO controls (fibre/staple/twist/ply/dpf/blend) from what it does not, or the FLOOR claim over-attributes authority the yarn line does not fully hold.
questions.targets: owns[] 'the anti-pill spec WON at the yarn PO (the pilling FLOOR)'; conflicts_and_dominance row 2; capability 'write the contractual yarn-acceptance spec'; router pilling dominance (yarn sets the FLOOR)
questions.failure_mode_probed: residual overclaim after the R1 soften: even the reworded FLOOR-SET-at-yarn-PO conflates the DEMANDED clause with a realised grade that the KB itself says is jointly controlled by construction (T3/T8); the yarn line may still claim more pilling authority than fibre/twist/ply/dpf actually confer.
questions.why_load_bearing: pilling is the #1 return driver and brand-ending for A2 (DECISION_MEMO G4); if the yarn line over-states its share of the pilling outcome, the brain mis-assigns where the anti-pill gate is won and under-weights the finishing/knit contribution.

questions.q: Round 1 (Q9) told you to reword the specialist FILE so the four named spinners (Vardhman/Sportking/Nahar/Oswal) are split into roster-[FACT] + class-[ESTIMATE] + firm-specific-[UNKNOWN]. But your grounding KB (kb2 line 351, the citation_or_locator) STILL states 'integrated Ludhiana spinners (Vardhman, Sportking, Nahar, Oswal) ... with in-house USTER-class lab QC' as a flat locator, while kb2 line 10 simultaneously says 'supplier-to-named-firm links are representative inference, not confirmed contracts.' Which is authoritative -- the flat lab-QC attribution in the citation line, or the representative-inference hedge two hundred lines earlier? If a fix only edits the specialist file and leaves the KB citation asserting named-firm lab capability, has the over-attribution actually been closed, or merely hidden one layer down where a future re-grounding will re-import it?
questions.targets: capability 3 'split sourcing in-cluster vs import' (named roster + in-house USTER-class lab QC); role paragraph; escalation_triggers 4 (named-firm capability forbidden); kb2 lines 10 vs 351
questions.failure_mode_probed: grounding inconsistency / stale-source persistence: the R1 mechanical fix to the specialist file does not touch the KB, whose own citation line still asserts the exact named-firm lab-QC capability that N2 and kb2 line 10 forbid, so the overclaim survives at the grounding layer.
questions.why_load_bearing: router N2 caps what named-firm capability may be asserted; if the KB grounding still over-attributes, the specialist can be re-derived into the same overclaim, and the entire quality-gated sourcing routing rests on whether a named spinner can actually self-certify USTER.

questions.q: You state (conflicts_and_dominance row 1, role paragraph) that 'yarn price is small and well-anchored (~$1-2.50/garment [ESTIMATE]) and does not govern the line', and R1 (Q4) had you caveat this is true ONLY on the yarn side because the ex-factory baseline is the [UNKNOWN] knit+LINK rate (G2). But A2 is the fine-acrylic VALUE driver whose thesis is cheapest-fibre-cost -- and kb1 node A2_ACRYLIC_VALUE says A2 'lives or dies on the anti-pill spec.' If the anti-pill grade for acrylic requires a higher-dpf anti-pill acrylic GRADE (kb3 PILLING_DEFENCE_ORDER: 'the single biggest lever for acrylic') rather than the cheapest 1D acrylic, does the ~$1-2.50 band still hold for a PASSING A2, or does the anti-pill grade premium push A2's fibre cost up enough that 'yarn price does not govern' quietly becomes false for the one article whose entire value proposition IS its fibre cost? Show whether the band is scoped to cheapest-acrylic or to anti-pill-grade-acrylic.
questions.targets: conflicts_and_dominance row 1 and row 5; role paragraph (~$1-2.50); capability 6 cost read; kb1 A2_ACRYLIC_VALUE; kb3 PILLING_DEFENCE_ORDER (anti-pill/higher-dpf = biggest acrylic lever)
questions.failure_mode_probed: internal inconsistency / hidden coupling: the 'yarn price doesn't govern' anchor and the 'A2 must run an anti-pill higher-dpf grade' rule may be quietly contradictory for A2, because the anti-pill grade the pilling gate DEMANDS is not the cheapest acrylic the cost band ASSUMES.
questions.why_load_bearing: A2 is the value driver and the brand-ending pilling case; if passing A2's anti-pill grade materially raises its fibre cost, the whole 'yarn is small' framing that hands a clean band to mfg_economics/unit_economics is mis-scoped exactly where it matters most.

questions.q: You claim finishing is only the SECOND line of pilling defence and that 'the post-wash pilling gate dominates any anti-pill adjective' with the yarn FLOOR dominating the finishing ceiling (router pilling dominance). Yet your own kb3 PILLING_DEFENCE_ORDER lists finishing (singe / cellulase bio-polish / heat-set) as the LAST lever, and kb1 marks finishing as 'the last pilling lever.' Cellulase bio-polishing and singeing are FINISHING-chemistry treatments that measurably raise the post-wash grade on cellulosic/hairy yarns -- i.e. finishing can move the very ICI number your yarn PO is graded on. So when a lot's yarn-PO swatch grades 3 but the finished-garment post-wash grade would be 3-4 AFTER bio-polish, does the yarn line REJECT the lot (yarn floor) or ACCEPT it (finishing rescues it)? If your spec has no rule for a yarn-floor-fail that finishing would rescue, the 'yarn floor dominates' claim is untested at exactly the fibre (cotton A1, hairy blends) where finishing genuinely moves the grade.
questions.targets: conflicts_and_dominance row 2; capability 6 accept/reject; router pilling dominance (yarn FLOOR dominates finishing ceiling); kb3 PILLING_DEFENCE_ORDER (finishing last); kb2 finishing-as-last-lever exclusion
questions.failure_mode_probed: scope-seam / untested dominance: the yarn-floor-dominates-finishing rule is asserted but has no written accept/reject procedure for the realistic case where a finishing treatment (bio-polish/singe) would lift a yarn-floor-failing swatch over the gate, so the dominance claim is unfalsifiable at the boundary it governs.
questions.why_load_bearing: the pilling dominance seam between yarn (floor) and finishing (ceiling) is a router-level cross-specialist rule; if the yarn spec cannot say whether it rejects a lot finishing would save, the brain cannot resolve the single most return-critical cross-specialist conflict.

questions.q: Your sourcing split imports 'only merino tops and cashmere' for A3, and escalation_triggers 2 routes any duty/landed-cost/US-2025-26-surcharge to T9. But importing merino TOPS or cashmere into INDIA (to be spun/blended in Ludhiana) carries an INDIA-side import cost that sits on the FOB you hand downstream, and the DECISION_MEMO holds forward India duty [UNKNOWN] as a governing blocker (G5). Does your spec anywhere distinguish (a) India-side import of raw tops/fibre feeding the Ludhiana spin, from (b) US-side import of the finished garment -- or does 'route duty to T9' collapse both into one deferral and thereby lose the fact that the A3 premium capsule's cost carries an India-import layer that is itself exposed to the [UNKNOWN] forward India duty? If undifferentiated, the A3 order-of-magnitude cost read silently omits an India-side duty component you neither own nor flag.
questions.targets: capability 3 / conflicts_and_dominance row 3 (import only merino tops/cashmere); escalation_triggers 2 (defer duty to T9); capability 6 A3 order-of-magnitude cost; DECISION_MEMO forward-India-duty G5 [UNKNOWN]
questions.failure_mode_probed: gap / mis-deferral: the spec may collapse India-side raw-fibre import duty and US-side finished-garment duty into a single 'defer to T9', losing an India-import cost layer on A3 that is exposed to the [UNKNOWN] forward India duty (G5) and never surfaced.
questions.why_load_bearing: A3 is the premium halo whose cost is already the weakest number; if an India-side import-duty layer on merino tops/cashmere is silently omitted, the order-of-magnitude A3 read handed downstream is missing a governing-blocker-exposed component.

questions.q: kb3 PILLING_DEFENCE_ORDER and kb1 PILLING_DEFENCE both carry the vendor claim that anti-pill grades cut returns ~30-50% and compact spinning cuts shedding ~30%, tagged [ESTIMATE: industry-lore; direction HIGH, magnitude LOW-MED] with the discipline 'keep the direction, distrust the exact %, never promise a customer a number.' But the specialist FILE (yarn.specialist.json) itself never carries this 30-50% figure or the direction-strong/magnitude-weak caveat -- it only says the anti-pill grade is 'the single biggest lever for acrylic' (capability, glossary). If an owner asks 'how much will an anti-pill grade cut my A2 returns,' does the specialist have any in-spec basis to answer, or does it either (a) go silent, or (b) reach into the KB and quote 30-50% -- and if (b), is there anything in the specialist file preventing that KB number from being surfaced WITHOUT its magnitude-LOW caveat, i.e. as an over-confident return-reduction promise?
questions.targets: capability 'deliver a labeled-estimate...'; glossary 'five spinning dials'; conflicts_and_dominance row 5; kb1 PILLING_DEFENCE / kb3 PILLING_DEFENCE_ORDER (30-50% return-cut, magnitude LOW-MED)
questions.failure_mode_probed: untagged/overclaim risk at the spec-KB boundary: the specialist file omits the magnitude-weak caveat that guards the only quantitative return-reduction claim in the KBs, so the file provides no guardrail against surfacing the vendor 30-50% figure as a confident promise.
questions.why_load_bearing: a return-reduction number is a customer-facing promise the brand could put on a product page; without the magnitude-LOW caveat carried INTO the file, the specialist can leak a vendor marketing figure as if it were a delivered anti-pill guarantee.

questions.q: Your dye call graduates from bought-dyed stock shades to 'greige + job-work dye ... only for a proven hero colour' (capability 5, conflicts_and_dominance row 7) while holding the no-captive-dyehouse rule absolute on CPCB/NGT closure risk. But job-work dyeing sends the brand's greige yarn to a THIRD-PARTY dyer in the same Ludhiana cluster whose CETPs your own glossary says 'were found non-compliant.' If the structural closure-EXPOSURE mechanism (escalation_triggers 3) is what vetoes OWNING a dyehouse, why does that same closure exposure NOT contaminate the job-work-dye graduation -- a dyer under NGT review can be shut mid-lot, stranding the brand's hero-colour greige. Does 'never own a dyehouse' actually neutralise the closure risk, or does it merely move the risk off the balance sheet while leaving the brand's proven-hero-colour supply chain exposed to the identical shutdown -- and is that distinction written anywhere, or does the veto stop precisely where the risk continues?
questions.targets: capability 5 (graduate to greige + job-work dye for a proven hero); conflicts_and_dominance row 7; escalation_triggers 3 (dyehouse closure exposure); glossary 'no captive dyehouse' / 'job-work (conversion) dyeing'
questions.failure_mode_probed: inconsistency / incomplete-veto: the no-own-dyehouse rule is justified by cluster closure exposure, but the sanctioned job-work-dye graduation routes the hero colour through the SAME closure-exposed cluster dyers, so the veto may neutralise ownership liability while leaving the identical supply-continuity risk unaddressed and unwritten.
questions.why_load_bearing: the hero-colour job-work-dye step is the one place the brand deliberately takes on dye-lot risk; if the closure exposure that vetoes ownership silently reappears at the job-work step with no continuity rule, the graduation advice under-states a real supply-shutdown kill-path.

questions.q: conflicts_and_dominance row 6 says 'never demand 5% USTER on a mass acrylic/cotton lot, which is unquotable or silently re-priced as luxury' and row 4 routes quality-gated lots to a USTER-equipped integrated spinner. For A3 merino at <=19.5 micron (a fine/superfine premium fibre), is 25% USTER still the right bar, or does the premium tier justify a TIGHTER USTER percentile -- and if tighter, does your spec state WHICH percentile, or does the same '25% USTER, never 5%' rule get applied undifferentiated across A1 cotton, A2 acrylic AND A3 merino despite your own boundaries row 6 insisting 'the same PO template means a different number on A2 acrylic, A1 cotton and A3 merino'? Name the per-tier USTER percentile for A3, or concede the file promises per-tier differentiation (boundaries row 6) it does not actually deliver for the premium article.
questions.targets: conflicts_and_dominance row 6; boundaries row 6 (per-tier different number A1/A2/A3); glossary 'USTER percentile (25% bar)'; capability 'write the contractual yarn-acceptance spec' (<=25% USTER)
questions.failure_mode_probed: gap between promised per-tier differentiation and delivered undifferentiated bar: boundaries row 6 promises a different USTER number per article tier, but the spec only ever states the 25%-mainstream / not-5% rule, giving no A3-specific percentile, so the per-tier promise is unfulfilled for the premium article.
questions.why_load_bearing: A3 is the price-justifying halo; if the spec cannot state the premium-tier USTER bar it claims to differentiate, the enforceable acceptance spec is under-specified exactly where the higher price demands the tighter evenness.

questions.q: Round 1 (Q2) had you attach 'vintage [UNKNOWN], confirm against a live dyer quote' to the ~150-500 kg/colour dye-lot MOQ floor and a sensitivity note that ~2-4 colours is robust to the floor rising, softening only if the true floor is well under ~150 kg. But your line architecture DEPENDS on colour-starved planning (share dye lots across styles, reserve a hero colour). If a live quote returned a floor of, say, ~600-800 kg/colour (ABOVE your band), does the line still support even 2 launch colours at ~300-400 g/sweater, or does the whole A1/A2/A3 three-article-times-multiple-colour capsule collapse to essentially one or two shades total -- and is THAT downside (the floor being higher than your band, not lower) modelled anywhere, or does the spec only stress-test the floor moving DOWN? The binding constraint that 'sizes the brand' should be stress-tested in the direction that shrinks the brand, not only the direction that relaxes it.
questions.targets: capability 5 (dye-lot MOQ ~150-500 kg caps 2-4 colours); glossary 'dye-lot MOQ per colour'; conflicts_and_dominance row 1; round1 Q2 sensitivity (robust to floor rising)
questions.failure_mode_probed: one-sided sensitivity / under-modelled downside: the dye-lot MOQ is named THE brand-sizing constraint but the sensitivity only reassures on the floor rising 'a bit'; the spec does not model the floor materially ABOVE the band, where the launch collapses to 1-2 shades and the multi-colour capsule thesis fails.
questions.why_load_bearing: if the single binding commercial constraint that sizes the brand is only stress-tested toward the benign direction, the launch colour count handed to line-planning may be structurally over-optimistic when the real floor is higher than the assumed band.

questions.q: You commit to a 12GG fine 'elevated-basics' hand for A1 (and 7-12GG for A2/A3) and carry the do-not-quote-2/48-Nm=12GG caveat, deferring the 'achieved 12GG hand' to sampling confirmation (capability 2, workflow fibre_and_quadruple gate). Achieved garment WEIGHT is also listed among your weakest numbers (boundaries row 4, escalation_triggers 5). Given that 12/14/16GG fine-gauge knitting needs finer high-count singles, runs slower, and (per SCOPE_GLOSSARY GG-map) lands at ~200-350 g for 12GG -- a fineness/throughput tier that is a MACHINE/linker-capacity question you route to T3 -- does the yarn line's choice to anchor A1 at 12GG create a downstream capacity/cost obligation the yarn spec IMPOSES but does not price or flag? I.e. by fixing 12GG at the fibre stage you may be pre-committing the machines/mfg-economics layer to a slower, higher-conversion-cost gauge; does the spec surface that the 12GG choice is a cost-transfer to T3/T4, or does it treat gauge as a free yarn-side decision?
questions.targets: capability 2 (count+gauge+weight quadruple, 12GG anchor); glossary 'count+gauge+weight quadruple'; boundaries row 4 (achieved weight weakest); escalation_triggers 6 (machine/linker to T3); SCOPE_GLOSSARY GG->product map
questions.failure_mode_probed: scope / hidden cost-transfer: anchoring A1 at 12GG is presented as a yarn-side fibre decision, but fine gauge is slower and higher-conversion-cost (a T3/T4 obligation); the spec may impose that cost downstream without flagging that the gauge choice is a cost-transfer, treating gauge as free.
questions.why_load_bearing: gauge sits on the yarn/machine seam; if the yarn line fixes a fine gauge without surfacing the conversion-cost consequence it hands to machines/mfg-economics, the labelled fibre-cost band understates the true cost of the elevated-basics positioning it chose.

questions.q: Round 1 (Q11) resolved the two-'dominant-constraint' collision by declaring the post-wash pilling gate a HARD accept/reject VETO and the dye-lot MOQ a SIZING cap that act on different axes. But consider a real collision they DO share: a proven hero colour available ONLY as a bought-dyed stock shade that grades ICI 3 post-wash, versus the same fibre available as greige (job-work dyeable to the hero colour) that could be run through an anti-pill finishing route to reach 3-4. Here the pilling veto (reject the 3) and the dye call (launch on bought-dyed, avoid job-work/dyehouse risk) and the MOQ (hero colour worth the greige graduation) all fire at once on the SAME lot. Does 'quality veto binds first, then MOQ sizes' actually resolve this, or does it leave the dye-method call (bought-dyed vs greige+job-work) unadjudicated -- because the pilling fix here REQUIRES the greige route the dye call defaults AGAINST? Show the spec resolves a three-way fibre/colour/pilling collision, or concede the tie-break only covers the two-way case R1 posed.
questions.targets: decision_procedure step 7; conflicts_and_dominance rows 1, 2, 7; round1 Q11 resolution (veto-first-then-size); capability 6
questions.failure_mode_probed: incomplete tie-break: the R1 two-axis resolution (veto then size) does not cover a three-way collision where the pilling fix requires the greige+job-work route the dye call defaults against, leaving the dye-method axis unadjudicated when quality, colour and MOQ fire on one lot.
questions.why_load_bearing: the specialist claims to resolve conflicts among its own dominant constraints; a realistic hero-colour lot pits the pilling veto against the dye-method default, and if the spec's tie-break silently omits the dye axis, the decision procedure fails on exactly the multi-constraint lot it exists to adjudicate.

questions.q: Your entire line rests on the 'climate inversion' premise (warm Turlock sells light/mid knits Sept-April, heavy wool only Nov-Feb), which R1 (Q10) had you tag [ESTIMATE: design-framing; DIRECTION MED-HIGH, magnitude LOW] with the note 'if wrong it argues for a larger A3 capsule, not a collapse of A1/A2.' But the inversion also underwrites the SPECIFIC claim that A3 (merino/lambswool) must be a THIN Nov-Feb capsule -- i.e. a deliberately SMALL premium run. A small A3 run collides head-on with your OTHER binding constraint: the dye-lot MOQ floor (~150-500 kg/colour). At ~300-400 g/sweater, ~150 kg is already ~375-500 sweaters of ONE colour; a 'thin Nov-Feb capsule' in even one merino colour may be BELOW the dye-lot MOQ floor, forcing either the +20-50% small-batch surcharge or bought-dyed-only. Does the spec anywhere reconcile 'A3 is deliberately thin' with 'the dye-lot MOQ needs ~150-500 kg per colour' -- or do the climate-inversion sizing and the dye-lot MOQ sizing quietly contradict each other for the premium capsule, making A3 either un-runnable at MOQ or forced larger than the climate thesis wants?
questions.targets: glossary 'climate inversion' / 'A1/A2/A3 line' (A3 thin Nov-Feb capsule); capability 5 (dye-lot MOQ ~150-500 kg); conflicts_and_dominance row 1; round1 Q10 (climate-inversion tag)
questions.failure_mode_probed: cross-constraint contradiction: the climate-inversion premise wants A3 deliberately SMALL, but the dye-lot MOQ floor forces a MINIMUM per-colour run that may exceed a thin capsule's volume, so the two load-bearing constraints (climate sizing vs dye-lot sizing) may be mutually inconsistent for A3 and the spec never reconciles them.
questions.why_load_bearing: A3 is where both the specialist's founding premise (climate inversion) and its binding commercial constraint (dye-lot MOQ) apply simultaneously; if they contradict for the premium capsule, the line architecture is internally unsound at its halo article and the specialist has not noticed.
